findings.title: Adding the first series never activates the visible-range translation
findings.description: The effect reads `seriesCountRef.current === 0` as a guard but its dependency array is `[mount.ready, chart, range]`. Refs do not trigger renders, and `chart.addSeries` only calls `series.onAdded()` (`src/chart/chart-facade.ts:44-50`), which mutates the ref without any state update. So when a consumer adds the first series, this effect does not re-run and the range is never applied until some unrelated dependency (e.g. `range`) changes. That contradicts the comment at `src/chart/use-chart-provider.ts:338` ("activates the moment it adds the first series") and the promise that initiative 120 needs "no other change to this integration". `src/test/use-chart-provider.translation.test.tsx:135-145` masks this: it calls `setRange(NEXT_RANGE)` after `addSeries`, so the passing assertion is really about a range change, not about series-driven activation. Either make the count reactive state (or expose it through the facade) and include it in the deps, or correct the documented seam.

findings.title: A failed `create()` produces a spurious teardown error against the real provider
findings.description: On a mount failure the catch at `src/chart/use-chart-provider.ts:303-309` calls `teardown()`, which unconditionally calls `provider.destroy()`. The real `LightweightChartsProvider.destroy()` calls `assertReady()` (`src/chart/providers/lightweight-charts-provider.ts:67-71`), and `assertReady()` throws when `this.chart === null` (`:79-84`). `create()` assigns `this.chart` only after `createChart(...)` returns (`:53-62`), so a throw inside `createChart` leaves it null. Result: two console errors for one failure — the real "provider create failed" plus a misleading "provider teardown failed". The spy's `destroy` never throws (`src/test/support/chart-provider-spy.ts:98-100`), and tests even assert `destroy` is called once after a failed create (`src/test/use-chart-provider.lifecycle.test.tsx:104-116`), so this path is never exercised with the real provider. Guard `destroy()` on whether `create()` succeeded, or make teardown tolerant of a never-created provider.

findings.title: `error` is documented as the first error but holds the most recent one
findings.description: The public `UseChartProviderResult.error` doc says "The first error from any provider operation, or null." `setOperationError` (`src/chart/use-chart-provider.ts:96-99`) unconditionally replaces `error` with the latest failure via `setMount((current) => ({ ...current, error: failure }))`, called from every `runGuarded` catch (`:121`). So a cascade of failures shows only the last one, losing the root cause the doc promises. `src/test/use-chart-provider.errors.test.tsx:234-248` is named "keeps the first error rather than being reset by a later success" but only checks that a later *success* does not clear the error — a second distinct throw is never tested, so the "first error" contract is both unimplemented and unverified. Fix the code to keep the first error (and add a two-failure test) or correct the docstring and test name.

findings.title: E2E comments point at the wrong spec and contradict the new build mode
findings.description: The newly rewritten header says "The chart itself is asserted in `chart-render.spec.ts`". That spec (`e2e/chart-render.spec.ts:13`) navigates to `/__chart-harness` and asserts the slice-102 harness with candles; the live product chart at `/` is asserted in `e2e/chart-live.spec.ts`, which this same change adds. Similarly, `playwright.config.ts:4-11` still claims "Specs run against the PRODUCTION build ... the same artifact `pnpm build` ships" and "Slice 102 extends this harness", which the new `command` at `playwright.config.ts:44` (`pnpm build --mode e2e`) and the comment at `:37-43` directly contradict — the e2e artifact deliberately differs from the production artifact. These are user-facing guide comments in files this diff touched; update them so a maintainer debugging the harness gate is not sent to the wrong spec or build.

findings.title: The mandated `setVisibleRange` failure test does not exist
findings.description: The "post-mount error funneling" block forces only `resize` to throw (`:220`, `:238`). No test anywhere forces `chart.setVisibleRange` to throw from the Context observer or through the facade: `src/test/use-chart-provider.facade.test.tsx:156-157` only checks forwarding, and `src/test/use-chart-provider.translation.test.tsx` has no throwing spy. The slice design (`project-documents/user/slices/103-slice.provider-react-integration.md`, "Operation-level failure handling" and Verification step 2) explicitly requires forcing `setVisibleRange` to throw and asserting `error` is set without escaping React. That is one of only three post-mount imperative paths, so its error behavior is unverified. Add an armed throw on `chartSpy.setVisibleRange` after a series exists, asserting `ready` stays true and `error` surfaces.

findings.title: Stale task-number and "built up across tasks" comments shipped in the new hook
findings.description: The file header describes work-in-progress state that no longer exists: "the forwarding facade (task 14)" (`:10`), "This file is built up across tasks 8/10/12/14 ... seams below exist from the start so later tasks extend one path" (`:16-19`), and "subscriptions join here in task 12" (`:185`) — even though subscriptions are already registered in the same effect at `:288-301`. A related inaccuracy: `src/routes/chart-route.tsx:31` says `readChartStyle` returns `undefined` "when a token resolves empty", but `:46-48` requires all three tokens to be empty; a single missing token yields a partial style object. These comments describe a construction sequence rather than the finished behavior and will mislead the next reader.

findings.title: Hook exceeds project size budgets and required a file-wide lint suppression
findings.description: The mount effect spans ~146 lines (three times CLAUDE.md's ~50-line function guide) and the file is 366 lines against the ~300-line file guide. The extraction into `chart-facade.ts` / `chart-operations.ts` reduced it but required turning `react-hooks/refs` off for the entire file (`eslint.config.js:75-78`), so future genuine ref-during-render violations in those 366 lines will go unflagged. The slice design records this as a PM-approved, documented overrun, so this is informational rather than blocking; a narrower suppression (or moving the counter callbacks behind a hook-shaped indirection) would restore the safety net.
